subtopics.title: The Mole-Ratio Method at Grade 11 Speed

questions.question: The coefficients of a balanced equation give the ratio of:
For N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, the maximum mass of ammonia from 28 g of nitrogen (with excess hydrogen) is:
When crossing the equation, the mole ratio is written as:
options: Coefficient of the wanted substance over coefficient of the given substance
Coefficient of the given substance over coefficient of the wanted substance
Molar mass of wanted over molar mass of given
Mass of wanted over mass of given

questions.question: Which quantity may cross a balanced equation directly?

subtopics.title: The Limiting Reagent — Who Runs Out First

questions.question: The limiting reagent is the reactant that:
options: Has the smallest number of moles
Is used up first and stops the reaction

questions.question: For 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, 4 g of hydrogen (2 mol) is mixed with 40 g of oxygen (1,25 mol). The limiting reagent is:
options: Hydrogen, because 2 mol of it needs 1 mol of oxygen and more than 1 mol is available
Oxygen, because 1,25 mol is less than 2 mol
Oxygen, because its mass is larger
Neither — the mixture is in perfect ratio

questions.question: In that reaction, the mass of oxygen left over when the reaction stops is:
All product calculations must be based on:
options: The reactant with the largest molar mass
The average of the two reactants

questions.question: Percentage yield is calculated as:
options: Mass of product ÷ mass of sample × 100

questions.question: A plant's theoretical yield of ammonia is 34 g and 27,2 g is collected. The percentage yield is:
A 10 g seashell sample with excess HCl releases 1,792 dm³ of CO₂ at STP (0,08 mol). The percentage purity of CaCO₃ (M = 100 g·mol⁻¹) is:
A calculated yield of 108 % most likely means:
options: The product is wet or contaminated with unreacted material
The theoretical yield was calculated for the wrong temperature

subtopics.title: Airbags and Explosions — Stoichiometry at Speed

questions.question: The airbag decomposition of sodium azide is:
130 g of NaN₃ (M = 65 g·mol⁻¹) decomposes completely. The volume of nitrogen at STP is:
To a chemist, an explosion is a reaction that:
options: Always involves oxygen from the air
Produces a very large volume of gas from a small volume of solid or liquid, very fast

questions.question: Nitrogen is a good choice of airbag gas because it is:
options: Heavier than air, so the bag stays down
Brightly coloured, so leaks are visible
Able to react with the sodium produced

subtopics.title: The Ingredient That Runs Out First

questions.question: Toasties need 2 bread + 1 cheese. With 10 bread and 7 cheese, the kitchen can make:
Bread limits the kitchen even though cheese is the smaller number because:
options: The recipe uses bread twice as fast, and only the ratio test decides
Bread is always the limiting ingredient
The smaller number is always in excess

questions.question: The chemistry version of the ratio test starts by:
options: Comparing the masses of the two reactants
Choosing the reactant with the biggest coefficient

subtopics.title: What the Kitchen Promised and What Reached the Plate

questions.question: The recipe promised 5 toasties; 4 reached the plates. The percentage yield is:
Which is NOT a common reason for a yield below 100 %?
options: Atoms being destroyed during the reaction
The reaction not running to completion

questions.question: Six toasties from a five-toastie recipe is like a lab yield over 100 %, which means:
options: The theoretical yield was a minimum, not a maximum
Something extra was weighed in — the product is wet or contaminated

questions.question: Purity is measured by reacting the sample with EXCESS acid so that:
options: Every scrap of the genuine substance reacts, while impurities do not react at all
The acid becomes the limiting reagent
The gas produced is easier to see

subtopics.title: The Pillow That Inflates Before You Blink

questions.question: An airbag inflates because a small solid pellet:
options: Decomposes into a very large volume of nitrogen gas in milliseconds
Absorbs air from outside the car
Burns with oxygen to make carbon dioxide

questions.question: 130 g of azide is 2 mole-boxes; the recipe pays 3 boxes of gas for every 2 of azide; each gas box fills 22,4 dm³. The bag volume is:
Engineers size the pellet by:
options: Running the stoichiometry backwards from the bag volume to the pellet mass
Trial and error with different crash speeds
Making the pellet as large as the steering wheel allows
Matching the pellet mass to the driver's mass

questions.question: Dynamite and an airbag share the same chemistry idea, namely:
options: Both need oxygen from the air
Both absorb energy from the surroundings
Violent, rapid production of gas from a small solid — the airbag just catches it in a bag
